players.product: 800G/1.6T optical transceivers + high-power ELSFP lasers (US-anchored manufacturing)

quarterly_data.signal: Orders and ramp sequence (CFO Stefan Murry): the 2 new volume orders for 800G single mode transceivers from the long-term major hyperscale customer that placed AOI's first 1.6T volume order in Q1 - 'We began delivering these 800G orders in Q2.' 'Looking ahead, we continue to believe that our 800G products will drive our near-term data center ramp, followed by our 1.6T products, which are on track to begin to contribute to our overall revenue later this year with the bigger ramp beginning in 2027.' On 1.6T demand beyond that customer: 'I think we have pretty broad-based interest among customers'; 'Until we have sufficient capacity to service multiple customers, we have to be careful about taking too many orders'; 'we definitely don't want to overpromise what we can actually deliver.' On 800G: 'our ability to deliver revenue in general, and specifically when it comes to 800G products, is limited by our production capacity right now. If we could produce more, we could ship more right now'; 'Clearly all of that manufacturing space has not been built out, doesn't have equipment in it yet', and AOI is 'going to continue to add more and more capacity really, most likely through next year'. CEO Thompson Lin: customers ask 'almost every week, every month, to speed up our delivery schedule', and AOI is working with several key suppliers to increase the volume in the next few quarters.
quarterly_data.figure: 2 x 800G volume orders delivering since Q2; 1.6T revenue from later this year, bigger ramp in 2027

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Thompson Lin on why capex is rising so fast: 'That's why our CapEx is so big, because as I said, if I promise any customer the laser like in Q3, Q4 2028, I need to start to spend the money, buy the equipment, buy the building, build the equipment. That's the reason our CapEx is increased so fast.' CFO Stefan Murry: 'our expansion planning has been underway for several years. We have already secured orders for long lead equipment and are partnering closely with vendors on delivery'; 'We believe that in the future, CPO will continue to drive increased demand for high-power lasers. We plan to continue to expand our laser manufacturing capacity in Texas'. CFO on the CPO laser: 'When we've talked to several of the major CPO customers, they love our laser'; 'It has nothing to do with customer engagement. It has nothing to do with performance of the laser or not having the design'; 'I would argue our high-power narrow alignment laser is the best in the industry, the best in the world right now.' CEO: AOI 'has been working on high-power laser, I would say six, seven years ago for LIDAR.'

CFO Stefan Murry on margins and earnings: 'while we do expect continued gradual improvement in gross margins, we continue to expect that the revenue mix in data center in the short term will be a slight headwind'; the foreign tax benefits and modest government subsidy income behind the Q2 non-GAAP net income beat are ones 'we expect to continue in subsequent quarters'. CFO: AOI is 'uniquely positioned to capture two distinct growth engines, the rapid AI-driven demand acceleration in our data center business alongside a robust runway in our CATV business', and its capital investments are designed to 'structurally lower our long-term production costs'. CATV: 'While the vast majority of our CATV revenue expectations for this year are related to our amplifiers, we do anticipate that we will generate some revenue from our software solutions this year.'
